transcript: This is GovExactate, but we bring you the federal stories that really matter. It's October 7th, 2022. I'm Ross John Fortuna. More than 10 years ago, the Stop Trading on Congressional Knowledge Act was passed by Congress and signed by then-President Obama. The law bars the use of non-public information for private profit, including insider trading by members of Congress and other government employees. In the decades since, enforcement of the Stock Act has been lagging and members of Congress have found their way through the box truck-sized loopholes in the law. In a recent business insider investigation, the site found dozens of dangerous conflicts of interests among members of both Houses of Congress and both parties, including Senator Dianne Feinstein and Tommy Tuberville and representatives Diana Harshbarger and Pat Fallon. According to data compiled by Open Secrets and Smart Insider, there are a dozen other members of Congress who have had some other direct financial investment in the defense industry while sitting on committees related to appropriations and the Pentagon. Members of Congress and good government groups like the Project on Government Oversight have been calling for a better congressional ethics law regarding stock trading. Pogo's Dylan Hetler-Gadette spoke to our show in August about the ways Congress finds itself outside of the rules.
